Goodpasture disease is a human autoimmune disease in which the target of the immune attack is the monomer M2 of type IV collagen, a protein that is a constituent of glomerular basement membranes.
the major Goodpasture antigen is the monomer protein M2* and that the Goodpasture antibodies recognize a site on the M2* molecule.
Goodpasture syndrome is caused by an autoimmune response to the globular domain in the noncollagenous domain of type IV collagens.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the antigenic site(s) in human Goodpasture syndrome.
the characterization and identification of the antigenic determinant(s), the nature of the antibody response, and the role of the antigen in the pathogenesis of Goodpasture disease.
the identification of the antigenic determinants of Goodpasture disease.

Goodpasture syndrome is an auto-immune disease directed against the globular domain(s) of collagen IV.
the Goodpasture antigen is a constituent of type IV collagen and is located on the globular domain.

the antigenic determinant of the Goodpasture antigen is a linear epitope in the globular domain and that the antigenic determinants in the Goodpasture patients are identical.
